summary: This script finds the highest numbered todo file in a directory (ignoring any status prefixes like DONE_ or PARTIAL-), then prints the next ID number padded with zeros. It scans all .md files recursively, extracts just the numeric ID from each filename, and outputs one higher than the maximum found.

explanations.2: This line makes the script exit immediately if any command fails, treats undefined variables as errors, and fails the whole pipeline if any command in a pipe chain fails — it's a safety guard against silent errors.
explanations.23: This assigns the first command-line argument to todos_dir, but if no argument was provided, it defaults to '.todos' instead.
explanations.24: Same pattern as the previous line: use the second argument as the zero-padding width, or default to 4 if not provided.
explanations.28: The find command locates all .md files and prints just their filenames (the %f format specifier), one per line.
explanations.29: The sed command strips everything from the start of the filename up to the first digit, then captures a run of 3 or more digits and discards everything after it — this isolates just the numeric ID from filenames like DONE_0042_fix_bug.md.
explanations.30: sort -n sorts these numeric IDs in ascending order, and tail -1 picks just the largest one.
explanations.31: This checks if highest is not empty (meaning at least one .md file was found), and if so, assigns that highest ID to the max variable.
explanations.35: The 10# prefix tells bash to always interpret max as base-10, preventing numbers with leading zeros like 020 from being incorrectly parsed as octal (which would equal 16 in decimal).
